title: Cluster Dependency Surfacing and Upgrade Impact QuickLens
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design a compact, contextual 'QuickLens' that surfaces cluster-to-cluster and tenant dependencies within Private/VPC consoles and previews the impact of a planned upgrade or maintenance window. The QuickLens should appear inline from cluster lists and upgrade planners and provide a digestible summary: affected tenants, downstream clusters, expected latency/cost delta, and suggested mitigation actions (canary targets, throttle windows, fallback route). Goal: reduce operator time-to-decision when scheduling upgrades and improve rollout safety for Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: QuickLens prototype exists for desktop and compact tablet widths with accessible color contrasts
Lens shows connected cluster graph (compact), affected tenant count, top-3 impacted services, estimated cost delta and SLO risk score
Interacts with the Upgrade Planner: selecting canary cohorts from suggested tenants updates the planner payload (mocked)
Design includes microcopy for thumb rules (when to schedule vs cancel) and links to runbooks
Security sign-off checklist defined and attached (KMS/PII considerations for preview data)
Usability testing with 6 platform engineers yields >=80% success on 'identify safe canary' task
design_notes: Focus on progressive disclosure: summary row -> expanded QuickLens -> deep link into dependency graph page
Use pre-computed estimates from runtime telemetry (latency p95 delta, tokens/sec throughput drop, egress GB estimate) rather than raw logs for speed
Risk scoring heuristic: combine percentage of tenants affected, SLO degradation probability, and egress volume to produce a 0-100 risk band with three suggested mitigations
We intentionally surface cost delta as a single-line estimate with a hover for breakdown (GPU-hours, egress, burst autoscale) to avoid overload
Compact visual: radial mini-graph for immediate glance + expandable node list for details
Accessibility: ensure keyboard focus order across QuickLens controls and ARIA labels for graphs
decisions: Choose aggregated estimates over live logs to avoid leaking tenant PII in previews
Initial rollout will be read-only (no automatic planner changes) until ENG implements mitigation validation endpoint
Show only top-3 downstream clusters by potential impact to keep QuickLens compact
Use a single 'Risk Band' CTA color system: green/yellow/red with explicit rationale tooltip
review_comments: PM (Sara Liu): Add a 'why this tenant?' callout when suggested for canary—operators need provenance
Infra Eng (Diego Ramos): Need a rate-limited backend endpoint; prototype should include a fallback state when estimates are stale
Security (Nina Cho): Confirm that tenant identifiers are hashed in the preview and make sure no raw IPs are shown
Research (Marta Nguyen): Recommend five short scenarios for moderated usability sessions focused on failure modes (network partition, KV cache cold start)
Design Lead (Omar Selim): Tighten microcopy for action buttons — 'Schedule Canary' vs 'Apply Canary' to reduce ambiguity
next_steps: Iterate prototype per feedback: add provenance blurber and hashed tenant IDs (owner: Jonah)
Coordinate with ENG to define rate-limited estimates endpoint and fallback contract (owner: Aisha)
Run 6 moderated usability sessions with platform engineers and capture task completion metrics (owner: Marta)
Prepare security review packet and include sample sanitized payloads (owner: Nina)
Schedule design review with PM and Eng on 2026-03-18 to align rollout mode
